enhanced.fullText:
The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) establishes comprehensive federal standards for protecting individually identifiable health information and regulates how covered entities and their business associates handle protected health information (PHI). Under 45 CFR § 160.103, higher education institutions may qualify as covered entities when they operate health care components such as student health centers, counseling services, or employee health plans that conduct electronic health care transactions.

The HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and E) requires covered entities to implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards to protect PHI. The Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subparts A and C) specifically addresses electronic PHI (ePHI) protection requirements. Universities must conduct risk assessments, implement workforce training, establish business associate agreements, and maintain compliance documentation under 45 CFR § 164.316.

Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) are mandatory under 45 CFR § 164.502(e) when third-party vendors access, use, or disclose PHI on behalf of the covered entity. The HITECH Act amendments (42 U.S.C. § 17921 et seq.) expanded business associate liability and introduced breach notification requirements under 45 CFR § 164.400-414. Universities must execute BAAs with cloud service providers, IT vendors, legal counsel, consultants, and any entity handling PHI for institutional purposes.

The Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR § 164.404) requires covered entities to notify the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) within 60 days of discovering breaches affecting 500+ individuals, with annual reporting for smaller breaches. Individual notifications must occur within 60 days, and media notifications are required for breaches affecting 500+ individuals in a jurisdiction.

HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR) enforces HIPAA through investigations, compliance reviews, and civil monetary penalties ranging from $137 to $2,067,813 per violation under 45 CFR § 160.404. The Omnibus Rule (2013) and recent guidance emphasize proactive risk management, regular security assessments, and comprehensive workforce training programs for higher education institutions managing student and employee health information.
enhanced.summary: HIPAA mandates that higher education institutions operating as covered entities implement comprehensive safeguards for protected health information, execute business associate agreements with third-party vendors, conduct regular risk assessments, and comply with breach notification requirements under federal oversight.
enhanced.requirements:
## Business Associate Agreements
- Execute written BAAs per 45 CFR § 164.502(e) before vendors access PHI
- Include required contract provisions under 45 CFR § 164.504(e)
- Conduct due diligence on business associate security practices
- Monitor ongoing compliance and contract performance

## Privacy and Security Safeguards
- Implement administrative safeguards including workforce training per 45 CFR § 164.308
- Establish physical safeguards for facilities and equipment under 45 CFR § 164.310
- Deploy technical safeguards for ePHI access controls per 45 CFR § 164.312
- Conduct annual risk assessments and security evaluations

## Breach Response Procedures
- Establish incident response protocols per 45 CFR § 164.408
- Document breach assessments and risk determinations
- Maintain breach notification capabilities for multiple stakeholders
- Designate responsible compliance personnel for breach management

## Documentation and Training
- Maintain compliance documentation for six years per 45 CFR § 164.316
- Provide regular workforce HIPAA training and updates
- Document risk assessment findings and mitigation strategies
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Breach notifications to HHS within 60 days for incidents affecting 500+ individuals per 45 CFR § 164.404. Annual breach reports due by March 1st for smaller incidents. Individual notifications within 60 days of breach discovery. Media notifications required for breaches affecting 500+ individuals in a jurisdiction.
